title: CAN (Controller Area Network) frame
summary: A CAN 2.0 frame: 11-bit (or 29-bit extended) identifier, RTR bit, IDE bit, DLC (data length code, 0-8), then 0-8 bytes of data, CRC-15, ACK, EOF. CAN FD extends DLC to 0-64 bytes with a different CRC. CAN is used in automotive, industrial, and aerospace systems.

structure.meaning: Message identifier (also determines priority; lower = higher priority).
Remote Transmission Request (1 = request data from a node with this ID).
Data Length Code: 0-8 bytes (CAN 2.0), or 0-15 (CAN FD: 0-8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 64).
Payload (up to 8 bytes for CAN 2.0, up to 64 for CAN FD).
ACK slot (dominant = at least one receiver accepted) + ACK delimiter (recessive).

ext.example_decoded: CAN 2.0 standard frame (simplified bit-level; shown as byte-aligned for illustration)
notes: CAN is a multi-master, message-broadcast bus with collision detection and arbitration.
CAN FD (Flexible Data-rate) supports up to 64 bytes per frame and higher bit rates (up to 8 Mbps).
CAN is used in automotive (OBD-II, CAN bus), industrial automation, medical devices, and aerospace.
CANopen and J1939 are higher-level protocols built on CAN.
ISO-TP (ISO 15765-2) segments larger messages over multiple CAN frames.
